text: {"headline":"99215 use is far above expectation and concentrated on low-complexity patients, but every documented 99215 chart supports the billed level, and widespread duplicate note text weakens that support.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing side points toward upcoding: 99215 share is elevated in every complexity stratum, and more than half of the 99215s fall on patients with zero or one chronic condition. Sampled examples include acute or follow-up diagnoses such as J06.9, R21 and Z09. The documentation points the other way, since all 17 documented 99215 claims supported the billed level. However, that rests on charts for only a small share of claims, and most returned notes were flagged as duplicates, which raises the possibility that cloned notes are propping up the billed levels. For example, C0214752 (a 25-year-old with no chronic conditions and a Z09 follow-up code) is documented at high MDM, which deserves a closer look. A reviewer should first compare the duplicate-flagged notes across patients for templated MDM and problem lists, then request a larger chart sample targeted at low-complexity 99215 claims."}
